title: S01.2 fix: a failed scheduled publish silently loses its schedule, and nothing in the product shows it
claim: publish_due() now isolates each due row in a subtransaction. The handler clears `publish_at` and writes a `content.publish_due_failed` audit row, and the code comment says this is so 'the owner can see it'. No admin screen reads audit_events: grep of `src/` for `audit_events` and `publish_due_failed` returns nothing, and COVERAGE C23 records that no screen shows the trail. The owner home shows only a count of scheduled documents (`AdminHome.tsx:144-152`). Neither `schedule_version` nor the browser `scheduleDocument` (`admin-publish.ts:109-118`, Zod plus media check only) tests the post-slug unique index, so the collision is only found at due time, in the cron job. `when others` also swallows transient errors (deadlock_detected, lock_not_available) and permanently drops the schedule for them, with no retry.
failure_scenario: An editor schedules post B (slug 'my-essay') for tomorrow 09:00 while live post A already uses slug 'my-essay'. schedule_version succeeds and the UI shows «مجدول». At 09:00 content_go_live raises 23505, the handler nulls publish_at and inserts an audit row, and post B never goes live. The scheduled badge just disappears. No screen, email or notice tells anyone, so the post stays unpublished until someone notices. A deadlock between the cron run and a manual publish of the same document has the same silent effect.
suggested_fix: Check the slug collision inside schedule_version for posts and raise unique_violation with the constraint name, so the UI shows the existing slug message at schedule time. Make the failure visible: show the latest `content.publish_due_failed` rows on the owner home, or keep a `schedule_error` on the version and show it in CollectionList. Consider retrying once for transient sqlstates (40P01, 55P03) instead of dropping the schedule.

title: A scheduled post that fails to publish (slug already live) silently loses its schedule; nothing the owner can open shows why
claim: AUDIT-1 S01.2 fixed publish_due so one failing document no longer stops the others. The fix drops the schedule and writes a 'content.publish_due_failed' audit row, and its comment says this is "so the owner can see it". No screen reads audit_events. grep of src/ and supabase/functions/ finds no reader, and PLANS/COVERAGE.md C23 records that no admin screen shows the audit trail. schedule_version (same file, line 188) never checks post-slug uniqueness, and the browser's validateVersion in src/lib/admin-publish.ts checks only the Zod schema and media ids. So the one condition that makes publish_due fail (the published_documents_post_slug unique index) is accepted at schedule time and then fails silently at due time. A publish-now gets the clear message «معرّف المقال مستخدم في مقال منشور آخر؛ غيّره ثم انشر.», but the schedule path gets nothing.
failure_scenario: Post A is live with slug 'launch'. The owner drafts post B with slug 'launch' and schedules it for 09:00. schedule_version succeeds and the UI shows «مجدول في ...». At 09:00 publish_due calls content_go_live, which raises 23505. The handler sets publish_at = null and writes the audit row. B never appears, the list shows B as an ordinary draft with no schedule, and the «المحتوى المجدول» count on the owner home drops by one. The only trace is an audit_events row that only the Supabase Studio SQL editor can display.
suggested_fix: Refuse at schedule time: in schedule_version, for collection 'posts', raise unique_violation if another published post already uses the same slug. The UI already maps 23505 to the slug message. Also surface the failure, for example by counting content.publish_due_failed rows from the last 7 days on the owner home.

title: Stale-version conflict raises 40001, which AUDIT-1 records as unanswered by PostgREST, and the 409 path is only tested with mocks or a direct pg connection
claim: AUDIT-1's own fix X2.3 (20260930120000_audit_fixes.sql:160-166) switched publish_version/schedule_version from a stale-tab error to unique_violation because, as its comment states, "PostgREST does not answer a 40001 at all: the call hangs". commerce_settings_save here, and commerce_policies_approve (20260927170000_policy_approval.sql:37-40, same `using errcode = 'serialization_failure'`), still raise 40001. The `admin` Edge Function reaches both through the same path: serviceRpc() calls serviceClient().rpc(), which is supabase-js to PostgREST (supabase/functions/_shared/db.ts), and admin.ts:370 and :389 then expect error.code === '40001'. No test exercises that mapping over PostgREST. tests/unit/admin-function.test.ts:315 and :383 throw a fabricated error with code 40001. tests/integration/commerce-settings.test.ts:144-168 and policy-approval.test.ts:135-151 call the SQL over a direct pg connection. So either the AUDIT-1 comment is wrong, or the owner's two stale-version conflicts never produce the documented 409 «تغيّرت الإعدادات من جلسة أخرى. أعد تحميل الصفحة.». I could not run the stack here (read-only), so I am reporting the contradiction and the missing real-path test, not a measured hang. The write itself is still refused either way, because the raise aborts the transaction.
quote: raise exception 'Commerce settings changed in another session.'
failure_scenario: Owner has /admin/settings open in two tabs. Tab A saves the seller name (version 3 to 4). Tab B, still holding version 3, completes the TOTP step-up and submits. commerce_settings_save raises 40001. If PostgREST behaves as the audit_fixes comment says, the Edge Function's rpc() call never returns an error, so the admin function times out or answers 500. The form shows no reload message, and the owner cannot tell whether the save happened.
suggested_fix: Pick one and prove it with a test through the real Data API (not pg and not mocks). If 40001 is answered, correct the audit_fixes comment. If it is not, raise a code PostgREST maps to a 4xx, as publish_version does with unique_violation (23505, mapped to 409), in both commerce_settings_save and commerce_policies_approve, and map that code in admin.ts:370 and :389.

title: Stale-version 409 for settings and policy approval rests on SQLSTATE 40001, which the repo itself says PostgREST does not answer
claim: audit_fixes.sql:164-165 switched publish_version and schedule_version to unique_violation because 'PostgREST does not answer a 40001 at all: the call hangs'. commerce_settings_save here, and commerce_policies_approve (20260927170000_policy_approval.sql:39), still raise serialization_failure (40001), and the admin Edge Function reaches them through the same PostgREST path (db.ts serviceRpc). admin.ts:370 and :389 turn 40001 into a 409, and operations.md:361-363 and :458-459 document that 409. The only tests are a mocked rpc (tests/unit/admin-function.test.ts:315 and :383) and direct pg connections (tests/integration/commerce-settings.test.ts:144, policy-approval.test.ts:135) that bypass PostgREST; no e2e test covers it.
failure_scenario: Two owner sessions save seller details or approve policies concurrently. If AUDIT-1's observation is right, the loser's request never gets the documented 409 «تغيّرت الإعدادات من جلسة أخرى. أعد تحميل الصفحة.» and the admin function hangs until its time limit; if the observation is wrong, the comment in audit_fixes.sql misleads the next maintainer. Either way the documented behavior is unproven end to end.
suggested_fix: Add one test that calls the real admin function (or PostgREST rpc) with a stale expectedVersion and asserts 409. If it hangs, raise a SQLSTATE PostgREST maps, for example unique_violation as publish_version does, and change admin.ts:370 and :389 to match.

title: Archive then republish resets first_published_at, rewriting the journal date and order
claim: archive_document() deletes the live row, and the next go-live inserts a fresh row with `first_published_at default now()` (`20260925120000_content_versions_and_publishing.sql:77,147-150`). The public journal shows `first_published_at` as the post's date and sorts newest first (`src/lib/journal.ts:84-85`). The column is named 'first', but it is only 'first since the last archive'. Hiding a post with `visible = false` keeps the date, and archiving does not.
quote: delete from public.published_documents where collection = p_collection and doc_id = p_doc_id;
failure_scenario: A post first published 2026-01-05 is archived on 2026-09-30 to fix a paragraph. The owner then publishes the corrected version. The journal now shows it dated 2026-09-30 and sorted first, above posts actually written after it, and its original date is lost. The audit trail holds only 'content.archive' and 'content.publish' with no date to restore from.
suggested_fix: Keep the first publication date across an archive. For example, store it in an `archived_at` or `first_published_at` memo that content_go_live reuses (`coalesce` from the prior value), or archive by flagging the row and excluding archived rows in the anon policy instead of deleting it. If a new date on republish is the intent, rename the column and label it in the admin so it is not misread.

title: media_usage lists every published document twice: as live and as draft
claim: The second branch of media_usage counts the latest version of every document as a draft. It does not exclude a latest version that is already the live one. When a document was published and not edited since (latest seq = published seq), it returns a 'live' row from the first branch and a 'draft' row from this branch. UNION does not merge them, because the state column differs. media_where_used passes both rows through. MediaLibrary.tsx:595-599 keys rows by collection-doc_id-state, so both render. docs/media-rights.md:79-80 promises one link per document with its state. The delete guard is unaffected, because either row blocks the delete. The defect is the misleading list. The integration test tests/integration/media-security.test.ts:325-327 uses toContainEqual, so it passes while the duplicate exists. AUDIT-1 did not report this.
quote: select v.collection, v.doc_id, case when v.publish_at is not null then 'scheduled' else 'draft' end
failure_scenario: The owner publishes a room or post that uses image X and does not edit it afterwards, so the latest version equals the live version. In the library, selecting X calls media_where_used(X). It returns (posts, <id>, 'live') and (posts, <id>, 'draft'). The panel «مستخدمة في» shows the same document twice, once with «منشورة» and once with «مسودة». The owner concludes an unpublished draft exists that does not. Every unedited published document shows twice.
suggested_fix: Add a forward migration with `create or replace function public.media_usage(uuid)` (same signature, grants kept). In the version branch, skip a non-scheduled latest version that is already live: `and not (v.publish_at is null and exists (select 1 from public.published_documents p where p.collection = v.collection and p.doc_id = v.doc_id and p.seq = v.seq))`. Change the integration test to assert the exact row set, so [liveDoc,'draft'] must be absent.

title: The exactly-once claim invariant is tested only sequentially; operations denial of media_where_used and media_rename_folder is untested
claim: The header (lines 13-15) makes the exactly-once ticket claim the core guarantee. The tests in tests/integration/media-security.test.ts:133-139 and 141-149 call media_claim twice one after the other. The second call sees claimed_at set and gets 55000 even if `for update` is removed from media_claim or media_complete. No test runs two claims in parallel (no Promise.all against media_claim, or two sessions with a held lock), so the race guard is unprotected. Also, media_where_used (role check at line 153) and media_rename_folder (RLS only) are granted to every authenticated user. No test calls either as an 'operations' or inactive staff member. The 'operations sees nothing' test at line 259 covers only direct table reads.
quote: select * into t from public.media_upload_tickets where id = p_ticket for update;
failure_scenario: A refactor drops `for update` from media_claim. Two concurrent media-complete requests for one ticket both read claimed_at null and both proceed to write the public derivatives. The failing request's cleanupAll then deletes the winner's `m/<id>/*.webp` objects, which is exactly what the header says can never happen. The suite stays green. Likewise, removing the role check in media_where_used lets an operations member list document ids and states, with no failing test.
suggested_fix: Add an integration test that fires two `media_claim` calls for one ticket with Promise.all on separate connections and asserts exactly one succeeds and the other gets 55000. Add tests where an operations user gets 42501 from media_where_used, and where media_rename_folder returns 0 and leaves the rows unchanged.

title: Contact intake cap (200/day, one notice per recipient) exceeds the notice drain cap (80/day), so a Turnstile-passing flood backlogs the queue FIFO and delays real messages for days
claim: contact_submit admits up to 200 messages a day (`contact:all`) and queues one priority-1 outbox row per active owner or operations member (lines 207-212). Priority-1 rows are drained only while v_sent_today < DAILY_QUOTA - RESERVE = 100 - 20 = 80. That gate is in this file's outbox_claim at line 291 and in audit_fixes.sql:373 after S04.1. Priority-0 receipts share the same budget. Claims are strictly FIFO (`order by o.priority, o.next_at, o.id`). Intake therefore exceeds drain by at least 120 notices a day with one recipient, and by 320 a day with two. The backlog grows without bound while the flood continues, and a real visitor's notice queues behind it. docs/operations.md:80-89 accepts the flood only as a form lockout and states 'nothing is lost — messages already stored still reach the owner's mailbox'. That reasoning ignores the queue backlog, and the owner-home warning is also silenced (see the previous comment).
quote: or not finance.rate_limit_take('contact:all', repeat('0', 64), 200, interval '1 day')
failure_scenario: An attacker who solves Turnstile 200 times a day, across 40 or more IPs at 5 per hour each and distinct emails at 3 per hour each, sustains the flood. With one active owner, the queue grows by 120 pending notices a day. On day 3 a genuine visitor writes to Anas. Their notice waits behind about 240 spam notices at 80 a day, so it arrives about 3 days late, and the delay keeps growing while the attack lasts. Anas's mailbox also receives 80 spam notices a day, and the owner home shows no warning. The docs claim the opposite.
suggested_fix: Make the intake cap consistent with the drain cap. Either add a per-day notice count to the contact throttle, so intake x recipients <= DAILY_QUOTA - RESERVE (for example about 40 messages a day with two recipients), or serve contact notices per sender fairly instead of FIFO. Correct the 'nothing is delayed' wording in docs/operations.md:80-89. This has to be a new migration, because this one is applied history.

title: Four every-minute pg_cron jobs and no purge of cron.job_run_details
claim: The repo schedules four every-minute jobs: content-publish-due (20260925120000:299), site-build-trigger (this line), email-outbox (line 253) and checkout-expire (20260927160000:1093). pg_cron logs every run into cron.job_run_details and never purges it. That is about 5,760 rows a day, roughly 2.1 million a year, each carrying the command text and status. The repo purges finance.job_runs (job-runs-purge, S17.1) and contacts, but grep finds no job_run_details cleanup anywhere in migrations, docs or scripts.
failure_scenario: After a year of uptime cron.job_run_details holds about 2 million rows of pure noise, on the order of 0.5 GB. On a small hosted plan (the free tier is 500 MB) that eats the database quota. It also slows every look at the cron history, and the small runid index grows with it.
suggested_fix: Add one daily job in a new migration: select cron.schedule('cron-run-details-purge', '17 3 * * *', $$delete from cron.job_run_details where end_time < now() - interval '7 days'$$);

title: Sign-in email declares RTL only on <html>, and the code paragraph flips to the left edge
claim:
dir="rtl" is set only on the element, and the three

elements carry no direction. Gmail web and the Gmail app discard the attributes of and , so there the Arabic paragraphs get an LTR base direction: they are left-aligned and the trailing ':' and '.' land on the wrong end of the sentence. Independently of the client, the code paragraph sets direction: ltr, so its text-align: start resolves to the left. Even where is honoured, the code sits at the left edge under right-aligned Arabic lines. Digits are Latin and the {{ .Token }} isolate is correct.
failure_scenario: Anas requests a sign-in code and opens the email in Gmail. The sentence «رمز الدخول إلى لوحة أنس:» is left-aligned with the colon at the wrong end, and «صالح لعشر دقائق. إن لم تطلبه، تجاهل هذه الرسالة.» renders the same way. In clients that do honour html dir, the code is left-aligned while the text above and below is right-aligned.
suggested_fix:
Wrap the body content in
and give the code

style="direction:ltr; text-align:right; unicode-bidi:isolate" (keep the Latin digits as they are).

title: A missing pages_deploy_hook makes publishing look successful while the site is never rebuilt, and the owner home cannot tell
claim: When Vault has no 'pages_deploy_hook', site_build_trigger returns false every minute and writes no finance.job_runs row. The local stack needs this no-op, but a hosted project that forgot or mistyped the Vault name behaves identically. The owner home then shows «بناء الموقع: لم يعمل بعد», the same text as on a fresh install with nothing published. The email path does not share this blind spot. There a missing Vault value leaves due rows, and emailWaiting warns «تأكد من الجدولة». The admin tells editors a change "shows within minutes" (ARCHITECTURE Publishing D32).
quote: select decrypted_secret into v_hook from vault.decrypted_secrets where name = 'pages_deploy_hook';
failure_scenario: On the hosted project the owner sets functions_url and jobs_secret but the hook is missing or misnamed. He publishes a post and sees the success message. Every cron run returns false silently, finance.site_builds.requested_at stays newer than triggered_at forever, and the public site never changes. Nothing in the UI, the job list or the audit trail flags it.
suggested_fix: When a request is owed (requested_at is not null and triggered_at is null or older than requested_at) and the hook is missing, insert one finance.job_runs row ('site_build', 'skipped', {"reason":"NO_HOOK"}), only if the latest site_build run is not already that. The owner home already labels 'skipped' as «متجاوز».

title: Stock-only variant saves from the admin still request a site rebuild, contrary to the stated design and the test
claim: The header comment (lines 94-96) says a stock change does not request a rebuild, and tests/integration/checkout.test.ts:941 asserts it. The trigger is a statement-level `after ... update of <columns>` trigger. In Postgres, `update of` fires when a listed column appears in the UPDATE's SET list, whether or not its value changed. It also fires when the statement matches 0 rows. The only writer of variants is the admin form. `TableForm.save()` sends `config.toRow(values)`, and variants.ts `toRow` always includes sku, title, fulfillment, price_halalas, enabled and sort_order alongside stock. So every variant save calls `catalog_request_build()`, whether the owner edited only stock, edited nothing, or lost a version conflict. The passing test issues `update ... set stock = 9` alone, which the admin never does.
quote: after insert or delete or update of product_id, sku, title, fulfillment, price_halalas, enabled, sort_order
failure_scenario: The owner corrects a signed edition's stock from 10 to 9 in the admin variant form. The client runs `update product_variants set sku=..., title=..., price_halalas=..., enabled=..., stock=9, ...`. The `update of price_halalas` trigger fires. `site_build_request()` sets requested_at, and within 2 minutes `site_build_trigger()` POSTs the Cloudflare Pages deploy hook and starts a full static rebuild. Nothing public changed. Repeated stock edits, or saves that end in a stale-version conflict with 0 rows, each burn a Pages build, and the build quota is finite. The integration test stays green because it never updates the way the admin does.
suggested_fix: In a forward migration, drop the update statement trigger. Keep the insert/delete statement trigger. Add a row-level `after update on public.product_variants for each row when ((old.product_id, old.sku, old.title, old.fulfillment, old.price_halalas, old.enabled, old.sort_order) is distinct from (new.product_id, new.sku, new.title, new.fulfillment, new.price_halalas, new.enabled, new.sort_order)) execute function public.catalog_request_build()`. Change the test to update every admin-sent column with an unchanged price and a new stock, and expect no build request.

title: The SQL cart-validation and money-bound branches have no database-level test
claim: tests/integration/checkout.test.ts covers the coupon math, holds, idempotency, throttle, concurrency and expiry. The refusal branches in `finance.checkout_price` that guard malformed or oversized input appear only in tests/unit/checkout.test.ts, which feeds fake rpc replies through the Edge mapping and never executes this SQL. Untested here are CART_TOO_LARGE (line 593, the guard that keeps `subtotal_halalas::integer` from overflowing), TOO_MANY_LINES (512), INVALID_LINE (519-526), INVALID_QUANTITY (532), DUPLICATE_LINE (536) and INVALID_DEDICATION (556). Also untested is the expired-token branch of `checkout_cancel` (line 1038). Nothing in the repo runs those branches against Postgres.
failure_scenario: A later edit to checkout_price (for example, moving the cart-size check after the coupon step) removes or mis-orders the 500,000 SAR guard. A 50-line cart of 10,000,000-halala items then reaches `(v_price ->> 'subtotal')::integer` in checkout_create and raises 22003 numeric_value_out_of_range. The Edge Function turns that into a generic 500 instead of CART_TOO_LARGE 422. An expired-token cancel could likewise start succeeding after a refactor. The whole suite still passes, because the unit tests only check the status-code mapping.
suggested_fix: Add integration tests that call checkout_quote and checkout_create with: 51 lines; a duplicate variant; quantity 0, 21 and '5' (string); a 201-character dedication; and a cart over 50,000,000 halalas. Assert the exact codes. Add a cancel test that sets access_token_expires_at to the past and expects NOT_FOUND.

verdict: split (verify first; fix only if real)
title: RECIPIENT_INACTIVE rows are counted and offered for replay in the admin, yet can never be cleared or replayed
claim: The S03.5 sweep marks a notice for an inactive recipient `exhausted` with last_error RECIPIENT_INACTIVE. `outbox_attention` returns every exhausted row (line 516). AdminHome.tsx `replayableCount` counts every exhausted or uncertain row as "needs attention". EmailView.tsx shows the «إعادة الإرسال» button for every exhausted row. `outbox_replay` always refuses these rows with 22023, because the recipient is inactive (lines 545-553). Rows are removed only by the contacts retention purge, about 90 days after the contact's sent notice, or by `privacy_erase_staff`. AdminHome.tsx:64-67 states the design rule that the count must be something the owner can bring back to zero, and this fix breaks it.
failure_scenario: The owner demotes operations member Sara to editor while 3 contact notices addressed to her are pending, for example held by the daily reserve. The next outbox_claim exhausts the 3 rows with RECIPIENT_INACTIVE. The owner home shows «مشكلات تحتاج انتباهًا: 3» and البريد lists them under «تحتاج تدخل». Each «إعادة الإرسال» click fails with «المستلم لم يعد عضوًا نشطًا…». The number stays at 3 until the contacts purge runs, about 90 days later, so a real email problem is drowned out.
suggested_fix: Do not surface these rows as actionable. Simplest: in `outbox_attention`, exclude `o.last_error = 'RECIPIENT_INACTIVE'`. Alternatively delete the swept rows, as privacy_erase_staff does for unsent notices, or make the UI treat that last_error as «انتهت» (ended) in `replayableCount` and in EmailView's REPLAYABLE_STATUSES check.

title: A QUOTA give-back keeps first_attempt_at, so a long quota wait turns the next ambiguous send into a manual replay
claim: The S04.2 branch gives the attempt back and re-queues the row as pending, but leaves `first_attempt_at` set by the refused request. The 23-hour idempotency window is measured from that column: the claim's uncertain rule at line 371, and `replay_needs_confirmation` at line 514. A 429 quota refusal is a definite non-send, so the provider never started a window for this key. After a wait of a day or more, and especially the monthly quota, which is probed once a day, `first_attempt_at` is already older than 23 hours on the first real attempt.
failure_scenario: Resend's monthly quota is exhausted, and a notice is claimed on day 1 with first_attempt_at = day 1 10:00. It answers 429 QUOTA and goes back to pending with attempts 0. This repeats daily for 20 days. After the reset, attempt 1 times out, or the dispatcher throws DISPATCH_FAILED, and the outcome is 'uncertain'. The row is now 'uncertain' with first_attempt_at 20 days old. The claim requires first_attempt_at > now() - 23h, so it is never retried, and outbox_due_since ignores it. The owner must open البريد and confirm a duplicate risk that does not exist, since no attempt was ever accepted.
suggested_fix: In the QUOTA branch, when `o.attempts = 1` (no earlier attempt could have reached the provider), also set `first_attempt_at = null` so the window starts at the first real attempt. Keep it when attempts > 1. Extend the QUOTA tests in outbox.test.ts with a multi-day wait followed by an 'uncertain' outcome.

verdict: split (verify first; fix only if real)
title: The upload-ticket cap is a concurrency cap, so an editor token can fill Storage faster than the sweep can empty it
claim: media_create_ticket counts only tickets that are still open and unexpired (5 minutes), so once a ticket expires the slot is free again. Each ticket hands out up to 5 signed upload URLs to the private bucket, and the bucket's 15 MiB limit applies to every part (declared sizes are checked only in media-complete). Nothing rate-limits media-ticket. The daily media_sweep removes at most BATCH x MAX_BATCHES = 100 x 10 = 1000 quarantine objects (media-sweep.ts:11-13).
quote: where t.actor = p_actor and t.completed_at is null and t.expires_at > now()
failure_scenario: A stolen or malicious editor/owner JWT requests 10 tickets, uploads 5 large parts to each and never calls media-complete. After 5 minutes the tickets expire and it repeats. That is about 50 objects and several hundred MiB every 5 minutes, and more than 14,000 objects a day against a sweep that deletes 1000. Storage quota (1 GB free, 100 GB Pro) is exhausted or billed, uploads then fail for the real editors, and the backlog keeps growing.
suggested_fix: Add a per-actor rate limit to media_create_ticket (for example count tickets created in the last hour, not only open ones). Raise or remove the sweep batch cap, or loop until no candidates remain. Consider an aggregate quarantine-bytes cap per actor.

verdict: split (verify first; fix only if real)
title: The failure counter is never reset by a new build request, so after exhaustion a later request gets one try and no retries
claim: failures only returns to 0 on a 2xx. Once it reaches 5, the else branch keeps triggered_at, so nothing retries. The next publish arms one attempt. If that attempt fails, failures becomes 6, `failures + 1 < 5` is false, and it is not re-armed. The 'up to five in a row' budget therefore applies to the first failing episode only. Every later request gets exactly one shot. The migration comment and I34 describe 'the next publish tries once more', so this exhaustion is known. The counter not resetting per request is not. There is also no way to rebuild without publishing something (site_build_request is revoked from authenticated).
quote: triggered_at = case when v_row.failures + 1 < 5 then null else triggered_at end
failure_scenario: The Pages deploy hook fails for a few minutes during a Cloudflare incident. failures = 5 and the request is dropped. Later the owner rotates the hook secret in Vault, and still nothing rebuilds. He publishes a post. The one attempt hits a transient 502, failures = 6, no re-arm. The post is live in the database but never built. The home shows «فاشل» until he publishes again.
suggested_fix: In site_build_request() set failures = 0 together with requested_at, so each request gets its own five attempts. Optionally retry a dropped request hourly, or add an owner-only rebuild-now action.

title: The S04.4 early-event fix misses a delivery or bounce event committed by a webhook transaction that overlaps the accept
claim: outbox_result's accepted branch reads email_delivery_events inside the UPDATE, which uses the statement snapshot taken when that UPDATE starts. email_event_record inserts the event and then runs its own UPDATE ... WHERE o.provider_id = p_provider_message_id (20260926120000:433-441) under a separate snapshot. The fix works only when the event has committed before the accept's UPDATE starts. When the two transactions overlap, neither statement sees the other's change: the webhook UPDATE finds provider_id still NULL and locks nothing, and the accept's subquery does not see the uncommitted event. Both commit and the event is applied to no row. No test runs the two concurrently (outbox.test.ts:355-388 inserts the events first). The window is milliseconds; I did not find a bigger one.
failure_scenario:
Row R is 'sending', lease L.
T_r (outbox_result(R, L, 'accepted', 'msg-1')): holds the row lock and starts UPDATE ... SET provider_id='msg-1', delivery=(SELECT ... FROM email_delivery_events WHERE provider_message_id='msg-1'); snapshot S_r has no event.
T_w (webhook email_event_record for 'email.bounced', msg-1): INSERTs the event, then starts UPDATE outbox WHERE provider_id='msg-1'. Its snapshot still sees provider_id NULL (T_r uncommitted), so 0 rows match and there is no wait. T_w COMMITs; the recipient is suppressed.
T_r finishes: the subquery used S_r, so delivery stays NULL. T_r COMMITs.
Result: R is status 'sent', delivery NULL, although a bounce event is stored. outbox_attention lists only rows with status in exhausted/uncertain/suppressed or delivery in bounced/complained/failed, so the bounce never reaches the owner's attention list.

title: publish_due and publish_version/archive_document take the same two locks in opposite order and deadlock on one document
claim: publish_due takes FOR UPDATE on the due content_versions row first (line 261), then content_go_live upserts published_documents (20260925120000:147-150). publish_version takes the advisory lock, then content_go_live upserts published_documents, then clears publish_at on content_versions (20260925120000:151-153), so it locks published_documents first and content_versions second. publish_due does not take the advisory lock, so the per-document serialization AUDIT-1 added for X2.3 does not cover it. The published_documents to content_versions foreign key adds a KEY SHARE on the scheduled row, which conflicts with publish_due's FOR UPDATE. archive_document has the same order (delete published_documents, then update content_versions). publish_due's `exception when others` catches the 40P01, so a victim publish_due row is silently unscheduled. No integration test runs publish_due against a second session: audit-fixes.test.ts and static-site.test.ts call it inside one rolled-back transaction, and publish.test.ts has no concurrent calls. A stale scheduled seq going live over a newer manual publish does not persist: publish_version's clear of publish_at either waits behind publish_due's row lock or makes publish_due skip the row. The interleaving below is the only bad outcome found.
failure_scenario:
posts/x has seq 3 scheduled for 10:00:00 and latest seq 4; it is live at seq 2.
10:00:00.000 T2 (cron publish_due): fetches content_versions(x,3) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so T2 holds V(x,3).
10:00:00.002 T1 (editor publish_version(posts,x,4)): takes the advisory lock, passes the stale check, content_go_live runs INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on published_documents(x), so T1 holds P(x).
10:00:00.003 T1: UPDATE content_versions SET publish_at=null WHERE ... publish_at IS NOT NULL, which waits for V(x,3) held by T2.
10:00:00.003 T2: content_go_live(x,3) upserts published_documents(x), which waits for P(x) held by T1.
Cycle T1 -> T2 -> T1. After deadlock_timeout (1 s) Postgres aborts one with 40P01.
Outcome (a), T1 aborted: the editor's publish of seq 4 fails with the generic 'تعذّر إكمال الإجراء.' while T2 commits seq 3 live, which is older than the seq 4 the editor meant to publish. The editor must retry.
Outcome (b), T2's subtransaction aborted: the handler clears publish_at on seq 3 and writes content.publish_due_failed {seq:3, sqlstate:'40P01'}. The failure audit row blames a slug or content error that never happened.
Swap T1 for archive_document(posts,x) (DELETE published_documents(x), then UPDATE content_versions) and the same cycle forms.
